newsitem.title: NORWAY: Orkla continues to drag down Oslo Bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Orkla continues to drag down Oslo Bourse index.

text.p: Shares in food-based conglomerate Orkla, Norway's second largest listed company, plunged for the second consecutive day on Wednesday to help push down the Total index at the Norwegian Stock Exchange.

The index finished 0.58 percent off at 1,175.69 points in moderate trade worth 954 million crowns. "The market is quiet today. It's mainly Orkla that is burdening prices," one broker said. "One reason is Procter & Gamble."
Norwegian news reports say the U.S. consumer products giant will set up shop in Norway and that Orkla is bracing itself for a tough fight with Procter & Gamble on its home turf.
The report added to poor sentiment in the market following Orkla's disappointing four-month results last Thursday.
Orkla's A share has since plunged around 14 percent. It closed 4.0 percent lower at 528 crowns on Wednesday and was the most traded share at 195 million crowns.
Industrial group Norsk Hydro, Norway's largest listed company, was the second most traded share at 68 million crowns. The share ended unchanged at 385 crowns.
